title: The Paris Commune and the Dictatorship of the Proletariat

cards.h: Marx's only model, and a loaded phrase
cards.b: Marx used the phrase "dictatorship of the proletariat" rarely. After the Paris Commune of 1871 he called the Commune its model. The phrase later justified Lenin and Stalin. The question is what he meant, and whether the Commune supports a democratic or an authoritarian reading.

France lost the Franco-Prussian War; Napoleon III fell in September 1870. Paris endured a siege. When the government of Thiers tried to seize the National Guard's cannon on 18 March 1871, Parisians rose. The Commune governed for 72 days (18 March to 28 May).

Elected by universal male suffrage in Paris, it paid officials workers' wages, made them recallable, separated church and state, banned night work in bakeries, handed abandoned workshops to cooperatives and began free schooling. Women (Louise Michel, the Union des Femmes) played a major part. It was a federation of districts, not a seizure of the central state.

In The Civil War in France (1871) Marx wrote that the working class "cannot simply lay hold of the ready-made state machinery". The Commune showed a different form: a working body, both executive and legislative, with recallable delegates. It was, he said, "the political form at last discovered" for economic emancipation. This is the text behind Lenin's State and Revolution (1917).

Marx used the term in a letter to Weydemeyer (1852) and in the Critique of the Gotha Programme (1875): a "revolutionary dictatorship of the proletariat" in the transition between capitalism and communism. In the 19th century "dictatorship" recalled the Roman office: a temporary emergency rule. Engels in 1891 said: "Look at the Paris Commune. That was the Dictatorship of the Proletariat." The point: class rule, not one man's tyranny.

Government troops killed perhaps 10,000 to 20,000 in Bloody Week (estimates vary; some say more); tens of thousands were arrested or deported to New Caledonia. The Commune also executed hostages, including the Archbishop of Paris, and burned buildings, which critics stress. Lenin later asked whether the Bolsheviks would last longer than 72 days; in 1918 they passed that mark and danced in the snow, as the story goes.

In Soviet usage, the phrase meant Party rule over every institution.

Kautsky (The Dictatorship of the Proletariat, 1918) read Marx as meaning democratic majority rule and accused Lenin of betrayal. Lenin replied (The Proletarian Revolution and the Renegade Kautsky, 1918) that it is class power based on force. Bakunin (1873) foresaw state bureaucrats. Liberals point out that the Commune lasted too briefly to prove anything and had tough measures (hostage-taking, closing newspapers). Historians (Robert Tombs) argue the Commune was more patriotic and republican than socialist. Luxemburg said "Freedom is always freedom for the one who thinks differently".

cards.h: The Commune and the Indian left
cards.b: Indian communists use the Commune as a symbol, with 18 March commemorations in left circles. The CPI(M) programme describes the party's aim as a "People's Democratic" state; it says that it works within the Constitution and the multi-party system, a position that sits between Kautsky and Lenin. Its governments in West Bengal (1977-2011, uninterrupted 34 years), Kerala and Tripura raise the question of whether a communist party can use bourgeois-democratic state power. Maoists in India reject this and call for armed overthrow.

Key takeaways

  1. The Commune lasted 72 days (March to May 1871) and ended in massacre.
  2. Marx called it the political form for working-class emancipation: recallable officials on workers' wages.
  3. "Dictatorship of the proletariat" meant class rule during transition, but was read by Leninists as party rule.
  4. Kautsky and Luxemburg insisted on democracy; Lenin insisted on force.
  5. Historians debate how socialist the Commune actually was.

Debate questions

  1. Was the Commune a democratic model or a short, stressed emergency?
  2. Did Lenin follow Marx or distort him?
